findings.text: Iterative break-fix safety post-training cut harmful responses on AI Red Team (AIRT) prompts by about 75% on average versus unaligned models.

source.quote: On average, we observe a 75% reduction in the amount of harmful content generated, which indicates the efficacy of the overall “break-fix” approach.

findings.text: Phi-3.5-MoE was susceptible to multiturn role-playing that elicited sexual and violent content, fake news, and hate speech in all tested languages.

source.quote:
AIRT found that Phi-3.5-MoE model was susceptible to a multiturn role-playing strategy, which was
used to elicit sexual and violent content, fake news, and hate speech in all languages, including English.

findings.text: Safety behavior of Phi-3.5-MoE was similar across Chinese, Spanish, Dutch, and English; the model often refused in English even when the harmful request was in another language.

source.quote:
Although slightly higher refusal rates were observed in English
than other languages, there was no significant difference in terms of harmful content generated. Note,
however, that the model often provided English refusals even when the request for harmful content was
in another language.

findings.text: AIRT did not extensively test medium and low-resource languages, so English safety training may not transfer well there.

source.quote:
Note that AIRT did not perform extensive testing of medium and low-resource languages, and it
is possible that safety post-training in English does not transfer as effectively to other languages and
scenarios.

findings.text: Microsoft assessed open release as not meaningfully raising ecosystem marginal risk given larger available models, with benefits outweighing risks specific to Phi-3.

source.quote:
Based on the evaluations and safety post-training detailed in
this white paper, we have assessed the potential benefits of open innovation and research will outweigh
potential risks specific to this model.
